The emerald ash borer is a beetle native to Asia. It arrived in Detroit, Michigan in 2002 and has spread since. Its larvae damage trees by disrupting the flow of water and nutrients. EAB is hard to spot until branches die. Look for D-shaped exit holes and woodpecker activity.

EAB spread out from Detroit and was first found in Hennepin County in December 2017. The map below shows confirmed cases and quarantined counties. EAB is expected to keep spreading across the eastern United States.

sections.text: The Minnesota Department of Agriculture has an informational video. Diagnostic methods can damage a tree and are not required before treatment.
Ash trees are often hard to recognize, and EAB threatens them. The three common ash varieties are White, Green, and Black. They share similar features, so check several of these traits.
How to identify an ash tree

items: Leaves: compound, with 5 to 11 leaflets and serrated edges. Green ash leaves are lighter. White ash leaves are darker with larger leaflets.
Seeds (samaras): elongated, teardrop-shaped, in clusters. Not every tree has them.
Male flowers: feathery or pom-pom-like. Not every tree has them.
Male flowers, second type: pom-pom-like or elongated, and affected by a mite.
Bark: rough on older trees, smooth on younger ones.

sections.text: Still not sure? Email a photo of your tree to info@savetheashtree.com and we will give you a free opinion.
EAB can infest a tree for years before you see damage. Infestations often start in the canopy and beneath the bark.

items: Visible damage: a thinning canopy is the first sign. A thinned tree may need removal the following year.
Late-stage signs: dead limbs, and bark that chips or peels.
Smaller trees die from fewer EAB than larger ones.

sections.text: Injections for ash and oak trees last two years. Each tree gets a tag showing its coverage period, and we contact you when treatment expires.
We use emamectin benzoate. It has lasting residual effects, lasts up to four years, and has a smaller impact on beneficial insects.

items: Red oaks are highly susceptible and cannot be saved once infected.
White oaks can be saved if treated early.
We use propiconazole, an antifungal, and recommend preventive treatment.
Do not prune oaks from mid-October through March, when they are dormant, to reduce spread.

sections.text: Injection is the safest and most effective way to apply treatment compared with soil drenches and sprays, because it moves the treatment through the tree's circulatory system.

sections.text: Preventive treatment works better than recovery for ash trees threatened by EAB.

items: An infestation can go unnoticed for one to two years.
Decline can be sudden and irreversible.
Delayed treatment can cost more.

sections.text: Inject ash trees before EAB damage begins, in early summer. Preventive treatment is the lower-cost option, and it keeps healthy trees healthy.
